capability.summary: Read the tenant trust graph
capability.description: Implemented. Read-only view of direct cross-application trust: applications as nodes and grants as edges, with the effective state (pending, active, expired, revoked) and expiry. An administrator with trust.approve sees every grant of its tenant; a writer with trust.write sees only grants whose provider application it owns. No query parameters: the tenant and scope come from the verified caller. At most 500 newest edges are returned; truncated reports more. See CAPABILITY_DIRECT_TRUST.md.

capability.summary: Accept one guarded pinned capability execution
capability.description: Opt-in guarded execution. C4B accepts only target and input and pins a published caller-owned composition. Every step rechecks original OIDC authority, active apps and independent same-tenant direct invoke grants; providers authenticate and redeem single-use step-bound tickets. C4B replay returns the durable reservation and never restores a lost lease or retries ambiguous work. Results require original consumer/subject/client and current authority. Success requires validated final output and confirmed Flowable history. No cancellation, resume, delegation or automatic retries. C4A retains its documented untouched-work replay contract. See CAPABILITY_COMPOSITION.md and CAPABILITY_EXECUTION.md. An optional context {purpose, dataSubject} declares why the call is made and whose data it concerns; it is bound into the idempotent request, sealed into the audit chain, passed to the provider on ticket redemption and listed for the data subject by GET /v1/me/data-access. When the context names a dataSubject, an active consent of that person for the consumer application, capability and purpose is required (403 subject_consent_required), unless emergency is true with a justification; emergency calls are queued for review and at most five may be pending per consumer (429 emergency_review_backlog).

capability.summary: List the caller tenant's audit events, newest first
capability.description: Implemented. Returns a page of the caller tenant's protected audit events, newest first, filtered by time. Requires a verified management principal with audit.read in its own tenant; the database function enforces the tenant and the permission. The response never carries tokens, secrets or request bodies.

capability.summary: Seal pending audit events and verify the tenant hash chain
capability.description: Implemented. Seals the caller tenant's pending audit events into a SHA-256 hash chain, then recomputes every sealed entry. A modified, deleted or reordered sealed event, or a removed newest entry, is reported in firstBreak; nothing is sealed on top of a broken chain. Requires a verified management principal with audit.read in its own tenant. The database administrator remains trusted; see AUDIT.md.

capability.summary: List the caller tenant's enrolled management principals
capability.description: Implemented. Returns up to 1000 enrolled principals of the caller's tenant and issuer with subject, issuer, managementClient, permissions and enabled. Never returns secrets, tokens or request bodies and never calls the identity provider's admin API. Requires a verified management principal with audit.read in its own tenant; the database function enforces the tenant, issuer and permission. No query parameters.

capability.summary: Read the tenant/application tree with current trust relations
capability.description: Implemented. Builds a read-only tree from real data: the root is the caller tenant (kind platform), children are the applications registered in that tenant (kind application), and relations are non-revoked, unexpired direct trust grants between those applications. Relation labels are the real published capability title, falling back to the exact capabilityId. There is no separate organization table, so applications appear directly under the tenant. At most 1000 applications and 500 relations; truncated reports more. Requires a verified management principal with audit.read in its own tenant. No query parameters.

capability.summary: Read one-minute traffic buckets for the recent window
capability.description: Implemented. Returns exactly minutes chronological one-minute buckets ending with the current minute, including empty minutes as zeroes, with requests, 4xx/5xx errors, average latency and maximum latency, plus totals for the window. Counters are real observations recorded as responses finish. They live in the Core process only, are per instance and reset when Core restarts; no database or persistence is involved. Metrics requests are counted like any other request. A verified management principal with audit.read is required. Query parameters are closed; unknown, repeated or malformed values return 400.

queryParameters.name: minutes
queryParameters.description: Number of one-minute buckets ending with the current minute.

capability.summary: Read the newest requests observed by Core
capability.description: Implemented. Returns up to limit of the newest requests, newest first. Each entry contains only the observation time, method, normalized path, status and duration. Query strings, fragments, headers, bodies, tokens, subjects and recognizable UUID/token path segments are never retained. The in-memory ring holds at most the newest 200 requests; it is per Core process and resets when Core restarts. A verified management principal with audit.read is required. Query parameters are closed; unknown, repeated or malformed values return 400.

queryParameters.name: limit
queryParameters.description: Maximum number of newest requests to return.

capability.summary: List capability calls that concerned the caller
capability.description: Implemented. Returns the newest 200 capability invocations whose consumer named the caller as dataSubject, with purpose, consumer, provider, capability and state. Any verified principal may ask, only about itself, in its own tenant and issuer. No inputs, outputs, tickets or operator identities are returned. Purpose and a SHA-256 of the data subject are sealed in the audit chain (event execution.subject_accessed).

capability.summary: List the caller's consents
capability.description: Implemented. The newest 200 consents the caller granted, with state active, expired or revoked.

capability.summary: Grant consent
capability.description: Implemented. The caller allows one active consumer application to call one capability about the caller for the listed purposes until expiresAt (at most 366 days). A C4A call that names a data subject needs a matching active consent unless it is an emergency.

capability.summary: Revoke a consent
capability.description: Implemented. Revokes one of the caller's consents immediately; calls already reserved under it lose their provider ticket at redemption. Body must be {}.

capability.summary: List emergency accesses
capability.description: Implemented. Emergency (break-glass) calls in the caller's tenant with justification and review state. Requires trust.approve.

capability.summary: Review an emergency access
capability.description: Implemented. Records once whether an emergency access was justified; sealed in the audit chain as execution.emergency_reviewed. Requires trust.approve and core-writer.

capability.description: Implemented application, capability-version and bounded direct grant approvals. Unsupported resource types fail closed; foreign and hidden IDs are concealed. See CAPABILITY_DIRECT_TRUST.md and CAPABILITY_REGISTRY.md.
